title: A new bi-polar deep-sea genus of Isopoda Bathyjaera gen. nov. (Asellota: Janiridae), including the description of a new species from the Jøtul vent field in the Arctic Ocean
content:
Abstract
Bathyjaera Kohlenbach and Linse gen. nov. is established for two species: the species Bathyjaera tyleri (Brandt and Malyutina, 2014) comb. nov. and Bathyjaera giselae Kohlenbach and Pereira sp. nov. The new genus is characterized by a broad body, absence of eyes, short antenna, peduncle article I shorter than articles II–IV, pereopods II–VII dactylus with small ventral claw, uropod exopod and endopod same length, wide pleotelson with a medial point in the caudal notch, short pleopods I with medial lobe triangular, and a bathyal distribution. Bathyjaera giselae Kohlenbach and Pereira sp. nov. was collected at the Nidhogg chimney (3016 m) in the Jøtul vent field and the deep-sea Amundsen Basin (4156 m) in the Arctic Ocean. The new species is designated as the type species and characterized by wide pereonites 4 (female) or 3 (male), spine-like setae on the posterior margins of pereonites (females), and spine-like setae on the dorsal surface of the pereonites (males). The analyses of COI and 18S sequences support the separation of the two species and the recognition of the new genus. Both species feed on bacterial mats and could be found on other specialized habitats, such as wood falls or cold seeps.
